evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 4: duo potentissimī rēgēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. possum)
terms.comment: Of people, cities and families with power or influence; with the genitive, master of (meī potēns, “my own master”, Liv. 26.13.14).
Strength of body or force (a strong man, a powerful remedy); mostly poetic and post-Augustan, rare in Cicero, never in Caesar, who would say valēns (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: when the powerful quarrel, the humble suffer
